findings.title: Date-override slots bypass busy-time checks
findings.body: When a slot's day matches a date override, checkIfIsAvailable returns true at line 133-135 before reaching the busy.every(...) check at the end of the function. Consequently a fixed or round-robin host who has a date override but also has a conflicting Cal booking or connected-calendar event during the override window is still reported as available, allowing double bookings on override days.

findings.title: Working-hours check never checks the slot end time
findings.body: Both start and end are computed identically from slotStartTime (hour*60+minute); slotEndTime is never used. A slot that starts inside working hours but ends after workingHour.endTime (e.g. a 60-minute event starting 30 minutes before the end of availability) therefore passes the check and is offered outside the host's working hours.

findings.title: Working-hours find logic rejects valid split shifts and accepts days with no availability
findings.body: The code uses workingHours.find(...) and returns unavailable if ANY entry for that weekday is outside the slot. With split/multiple working-hour ranges on the same day, a slot valid in the second range is rejected because it is outside the first. Conversely, if no entry includes slotStartTime.day(), find returns undefined and execution falls through to the busy check, so a host with no working hours that day is treated as available — defeating the per-fixed-host check this PR adds, since getTimeSlots only receives aggregated hours.

findings.title: Multiple date overrides on the same day are handled incorrectly
findings.body: dateOverrides.find(...) stops at the first override for which the callback returns true, and the callback returns true when the slot is OUTSIDE that override. With two override ranges on the same day, a slot inside the first range but outside the second makes find succeed and the function returns false, incorrectly hiding slots that are inside one of the day's overrides.

findings.title: Zero-length date override comparison uses object identity
findings.body: dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...) compares two distinct Dayjs objects with ===, which is always false. The intended special case for an empty override (start equals end, i.e. unavailable all day) is therefore never detected via this branch and relies on accidental fall-through of the surrounding comparisons, so empty overrides are not reliably honoured.

findings.title: Override conversion assumes timeZone is present and loses day overflow
findings.body: override.timeZone is optional in the TimeRange type (packages/types/schedule.d.ts), but line 212-213 unconditionally calls .tz(override.timeZone); callers passing overrides without timeZone get a guessed/default timezone offset and wrong slots. Additionally startTime/endTime are reduced to hour*60+minute after adding the offset, so an override pushed past midnight by the offset wraps to a small minute value, producing endTime <= startTime which buildSlots discards (start >= end), causing override availability near midnight in another timezone to disappear rather than appear on the correct invitee day.

findings.title: No test for the round-robin fixed-host date override fix
findings.body: The PR description states the main fix is that fixed hosts' date overrides constrain round-robin events, but the only added test exercises a personal event in a different invitee timezone. There is no scenario with schedulingType ROUND_ROBIN, a fixed host with a date override, and a loose host, verifying that slots outside the fixed host's override are hidden and slots inside it remain — so the new checkIfIsAvailable fixed-host path (including its busy-time and working-hours behaviour) is untested and regressions would not be caught.
